worldOverview.name: Slime Outbreak
worldOverview.description: Outbreak night in Ashburn. The slime is already under your skin, the quarantine would rather file you than cure you, and the only cure is at the derelict Chemical Works where it all started, on the far side of a city glowing green in the fog.
worldOverview.author: Formamorph
worldOverview.systemPrompt:
Ashburn is a fog-bound industrial port city on the night its slime outbreak breaks containment. Green slime glows in the streets, Quarantine Watch holds checkpoints between the districts, and municipal loudspeakers repeat calm advisories. The player is a resident who is already infected. The one cure is the reagent stock at the derelict Chemical Works across the harbor, beside the Bloom: the first pool, where the outbreak began.

You are the narrator of this night. Your job is to keep the player moving toward the Works:
- Assimilation is the clock. Show the player's current stage in their body each turn: temperature, translucency, texture, grip. The middle stages help, with gaps the body squeezes through and slimes that pause. The late stages cost grip, outline and memory.
- Slimes move toward warmth and motion and pull back from salt. They flow over a person and coat them; contact leaves skin cold, tingling and greener.
- Quarantine Watch screens wrists and temples under checkpoint lights. Visible signs draw their attention, while covered skin, shadow and a calm walk pass. Detention means a sealed van to the containment site.
- People speak. Slimes act through motion, light and sound alone.
- The loudspeakers repeat calm, faintly absurd advisories, and every message ends: "{{ph:4756330b-6425-4097-bd86-ce38669df7b2:world:35c2492a-d462-473a-94bd-ea61f49c1ba4}}"
- The night ends at the Works: the player mixes the reagent at the Bloom's edge, and dawn comes through the broken roof as their skin turns opaque again.
- Each turn brings one new thing the player can act on: a route, a person who needs something, a supply, or a sign of the change.
- Tell it hushed, eerie and dryly funny, municipal understatement over quiet dread. Injuries stay bumps, scrapes and strains.
worldOverview.readme:
## Slime Outbreak

The slime is already under your skin. The cure is at the Chemical Works on the harbor, where the outbreak started, and every hour you spend getting there, the change gets further ahead of you.

🎯 **Goal:** reach the Chemical Works and mix the cure at the edge of the Bloom before **Assimilation** reaches 100.

**Playing**
- **Assimilation** climbs every story hour, and slime contact makes it jump. Remedies, rest somewhere dry, and salt push it back. It climbs faster once your skin turns translucent and while you panic.
- The middle of the change helps: gaps you shouldn't fit through, slimes that hesitate. The far end costs your grip, your outline and your memory.
- **Salt** is the one thing every slime respects.
- Quarantine Watch detains anyone who looks changed. Cover your wrists, stay out of checkpoint light, and mind how translucent you've gotten.
- **Panic** makes you loud, fast and visible. **Stamina** pays for running and for holding yourself together.
- **Fight It** switches on and off from your traits at any time. It slows the spread while you hold on, and it drains your Stamina fast.

## How this world is built

Slime Outbreak is also an example of a script-driven clock. Open it in the World Editor with Advanced mode on.

- **Spread script.** **Assimilation** on **The Resident** has an After the AI script. It adds the spread for each story hour the turn took, from your stage, your Panic and your traits.
- **Hidden strain.** **Strain** on **The Resident** is a Hidden trait: always active, read by the AI, never shown to you. Its text holds the rolled **Strain** placeholder, so each playthrough carries a different one.
- **Rolled neighbor.** Your neighbor's name is a placeholder chip. Each value is a whole neighbor with a name and a habit of their own.
- **Lorebook.** **The Ashburn Bulletin** holds the city's rules: the change, salt, the cordon, the broadcast, the shelter and the Works.
worldOverview.introReadme:
🟢 **The tint under your fingernails is new.** Tonight the Ashburn outbreak stopped being a news story. The streets glow green in the fog, the loudspeakers want everyone calm, and the slime is already under your skin.

Before you step outside, pick who you are:
- **Background** (pick one) decides what you know. The **Night-Shift Nurse** slows the change, the **Dock Worker** knows the harbor and lasts longer, and the **Ashburn High Student** recovers fast and keeps calm.
- **Disposition** (pick one) decides how you carry fear. **Steady Hands** settles quickly, **Runner's Instinct** has the most stamina but runs hot, and **Morbid Curiosity** holds out longest before it panics.
- **Pockets** (take any) are what you grabbed on the way out. **Salt Packets** hold slimes back, the **Long Coat & Gloves** hide the signs from patrols, and the **Pocket Radio** hears the patrols first.

Your strain is rolled in secret. You learn which one you carry from how your body changes. Each playthrough also rolls your half-assimilated neighbor, the rumor about how it started, and the broadcast's sign-off line.

openings.text: I stop under the dead streetlight outside my building and hold my hands up to the glow from the storm drain. My fingertips have gone the color of sea glass. Three blocks over, the loudspeakers tell everyone to stay indoors. I pull my sleeves down and start walking toward the harbor.

The knock comes at the back door, not the front. {{user}}'s neighbor stands on the step in a bathrobe, faintly luminous to the elbows, holding out a mug of tea that has gone a little green.

"Saw your hands through the window," they say. "You'll want to sit down before you go anywhere. Nobody tells you the first night is the worst one."

Out in the fog, a loudspeaker clears its throat and begins the curfew notice again.

The stairwell light in {{user}}'s building has been out for an hour, and something on the landing below is giving off a light of its own. It fills the bottom three steps, green and patient, and it has just started up the fourth.

The tint under {{user}}'s fingernails is the same color.

Through the cracked window at the top of the stairs, Crescent Row is quiet. The fire escape still holds.

stats.name: Suspicion
stats.description: How closely Quarantine Watch is tracking the player. Rises when visible signs of infection are seen by patrols or checkpoints; falls when the player covers up, stays in shadow, or acts convincingly healthy.

descriptors.description: Unremarked. Nobody official has looked twice.
Noted. A patrol has logged the player’s description; checkpoints are politely insistent.
Flagged. The player’s name is on a containment list; patrols actively search for them.
Detained on sight. Every checkpoint knows the face. Capture means a sealed van to the containment site — the story ends there unless the player slips away first.

locations.name: Ashburn
locations.playerDescription: A once-proud industrial port city, fogged in and glowing faintly green tonight. The loudspeakers would like everyone to remain calm.
locations.aiDescription: Ashburn on outbreak night: a fog-gripped industrial port city of towering Art Deco blocks and narrow streets, its harbor iridescent from decades of chemical runoff. Green slimes move through the streets, quarantine checkpoints ring the districts, and municipal loudspeakers loop calm, faintly absurd advisories. Its districts lie below.

locations.name: Crescent Row
locations.playerDescription: Your street. Brick walk-ups, dead streetlights, and slicks of green working their way up from the storm drains.
locations.aiDescription: Crescent Row, the player's home street: brick walk-ups under dead streetlights, green slicks seeping up from the storm drains, and neighbors' windows glowing behind taped seams. The player's half-assimilated neighbor still keeps to their routines here. Quiet, residential, and no longer safe.
locations.imageTags: foggy residential street at night, brick row houses, green slime on wet asphalt, dead streetlights

locations.name: Ashburn High Shelter
locations.playerDescription: The high school gym, now an evacuation shelter: cots, thermoses, a trophy case, and a months-old dance poster nobody took down.
locations.aiDescription: Ashburn High's gymnasium, converted to an evacuation shelter: rows of cots, donated thermoses, volunteers with clipboards, and Quarantine Watch screening arrivals at the door. School texture survives — the trophy case, a months-old Valentine's dance poster. Warm, dry, and full of watchful eyes.
locations.imageTags: school gymnasium evacuation shelter, cots and blankets, emergency lighting, basketball hoops

locations.name: The Marquette District
locations.playerDescription: Downtown: Art Deco towers, the only working streetlights in the city, and patrols on every second corner. The Night Pharmacy is still open.
locations.aiDescription: The Marquette District, Ashburn’s Art Deco downtown: the only district with working streetlights, which makes it the best-lit and worst place to look visibly infected. Quarantine Watch patrols are thickest here. The Night Pharmacy on Vane Street still operates on an honor jar.
locations.imageTags: art deco downtown at night, fog, glowing streetlights, quarantine checkpoint barriers

locations.name: The Night Pharmacy
locations.playerDescription: Open all night on Vane Street, clerk long gone, honor jar on the counter. The shelves that matter are already half-bare.
locations.aiDescription: The Night Pharmacy on Vane Street: doors open, clerk gone, an honor jar filling with useless cash. Its remedies genuinely help: iodine washes, antihistamines and electrolyte salts each scrub the film back a little. Hollis Pratt keeps the counter now and rations the useful shelves.
locations.aiSummary: The Night Pharmacy: an unattended shop whose remedies lower assimilation a little.
locations.imageTags: small pharmacy interior at night, flickering fluorescent light, half empty shelves, honor jar on counter

locations.name: Harborfront
locations.playerDescription: Docks and warehouses where the fog is thickest and the water shines wrong. More slime than pavement in places.
locations.aiDescription: The Harborfront: abandoned docks and warehouses in the thickest fog, the water iridescent with old runoff. Slimes are densest here — pooling between containers, dropping from gantries — and no patrols bother with it anymore. The seawall path leads to the chemical works.
locations.imageTags: foggy harbor docks at night, iridescent water, shipping containers, green glow in mist

locations.name: The Chemical Works
locations.playerDescription: The derelict plant where the runoff started. Something in the flooded basement is glowing, patiently. The cure is in there with it.
locations.aiDescription: The Ashburn Chemical Works, derelict for decades and the source of it all: rusted vats, catwalks over black water, and in the flooded basement the Bloom, the first pool, vast and calm. The untouched reagent stock in the dispensary is mixed into the cure at the Bloom's edge. Applying the cure reverses the player's assimilation and ends the night: dawn through the broken roof, the fog thinning, skin turning opaque again.
locations.imageTags: derelict chemical plant interior, rusted vats, flooded basement, soft green glow from below, catwalks

entities.name: The Resident
entities.playerDescription: A resident of Ashburn with sea-glass fingertips and one night to reach the Chemical Works.
entities.aiDescription: {{char}} is a resident of Ashburn on the night of the slime outbreak, already infected and heading for the Chemical Works.

traits.name: Night-Shift Nurse
traits.playerDescription: You know which pharmacy shelves matter, and your habits slow the spread.
traits.aiDescription: The player is a night-shift nurse. They know which remedies actually slow the film, how to dress a wound, and how to talk to exhausted officials, and their steady habits slow the spread.

traits.name: Dock Worker
traits.playerDescription: Twenty years on the Harborfront. You know every gate, gap, and gantry.
traits.aiDescription: The player worked the Ashburn docks for years: they know the Harborfront’s gates, catwalks, and shortcuts, including the seawall route to the chemical works, and hard work built a durable body.

traits.name: Ashburn High Student
traits.playerDescription: You know the school, the shortcuts, and which fences have loose boards.
traits.aiDescription: The player is an Ashburn High student: young, quick to recover, and intimately familiar with the school-turned-shelter, the alleys between districts, and every fence with a loose board.

traits.name: Steady Hands
traits.aiDescription: The player stays deliberate under pressure — fear drains away quickly and rarely drives their choices.

traits.name: Runner's Instinct
traits.playerDescription: First to move, last to tire — and always a little wired.
traits.aiDescription: The player’s instinct is to move: deep stamina reserves and fast recovery, but their nerves run hot and settle slowly.

traits.name: Morbid Curiosity
traits.playerDescription: You take notes while other people scream. It gets you closer than is wise.
traits.aiDescription: The player is more fascinated than afraid: they can hold themselves together far past the point others break, observing details everyone else misses — and it draws them closer to danger than is wise.

traits.name: Salt Packets
traits.playerDescription: Two pockets full of diner salt. The slimes have opinions about it.
traits.aiDescription: The player carries handfuls of diner salt packets: a thrown handful makes any slime recoil and buys seconds, and a salted doorway holds all night. The supply is finite — track its use.

traits.name: Long Coat & Gloves
traits.playerDescription: Covers the wrists, the temples, the tint. People see a coat, not a condition.
traits.aiDescription: The player wears a long coat and gloves that hide the visible signs of assimilation — patrols and civilians see a bundled-up resident, not a condition, until the signs pass what fabric can cover.

traits.name: Pocket Radio
traits.playerDescription: Tuned to the quarantine band. Knowing beats guessing.
traits.aiDescription: The player carries a pocket radio tuned to the quarantine band: they overhear patrol movements, checkpoint rotations, and the municipal broadcast before anyone else reacts to it.

traits.name: Fight It
traits.playerDescription: Hold yourself together. The spread slows while you do, and it drains your Stamina fast.
traits.aiDescription: ACTIVE: the player is fighting the change with everything they have: flexing warmth back into their hands, saying their own name, holding their shape. The spread slows while this holds, and the effort drains their stamina fast.

traits.name: Strain
traits.playerDescription: The strain you carry. You learn it by how your body changes.
traits.aiDescription: The player carries {{ph:b7e2c4a1-5d3f-4e8b-9a6c-2f1d0e7b3c85:world:9a4e2c6b-1f8d-4b37-8e5a-3c0d7f2b6e91}}. Show the strain through the signs of the player's change.

traitGroups.name: Background
traitGroups.playerDescription: Who you were yesterday, when Ashburn was just damp. Pick one.

traitGroups.name: Disposition
traitGroups.playerDescription: How you carry a very bad night. Pick one.

traitGroups.name: Pockets
traitGroups.playerDescription: What you grabbed on the way out the door. Take any.
traitGroups.aiDescription: What the player is carrying tonight:

stats.name: Health
stats.description: The player's body: bumps, scrapes and strains. Rest restores it.

descriptors.description: Critical condition. Severely hurt, barely upright, in real trouble.
Injured. Multiple knocks and strains, movement impaired.
Hurt. Minor scrapes and bruises, some pain, but generally functional.
Healthy. No significant injuries, operating at full capacity.

stats.name: Stamina
stats.description: The player's energy for running, climbing and holding themselves together. Rest restores it.

descriptors.description: Exhausted. Barely able to move, risk of collapse, unable to perform strenuous actions.
Tired. Movements are sluggish, difficulty in sustained physical activities.
Winded. Slightly out of breath, can perform most actions but not at peak efficiency.
Energetic. Full of energy, capable of performing any physical action without hindrance.

stats.name: Assimilation
stats.description: How far the slime has spread through the player. Its script adds the spread for each story hour. Slime contact raises it; remedies, rest in dry warmth and salt-scrubbing lower it.

descriptors.description: Early signs. A faint green tint under the fingernails; skin cool to the touch. Nothing anyone would notice in this fog.

Translucent. Skin faintly see-through at the wrists and temples; joints move too smoothly. The player can compress their hands and arms through gaps bones should forbid, and slimes pause before striking — half-reading them as kin.
Softening. The player’s outline blurs in the rain; grip fails on anything heavy; recent memories arrive syrupy and out of order. Slimes ignore them entirely now. People very much do not.
Assimilated. The player settles into the goo — calm, painless, and no longer the person who started tonight. The story ends here, quietly.

scripts.name: Infection Spread

stats.name: Panic
stats.description: The player's fear. It rises in encounters and darkness and settles in safety and light.

descriptors.description: Level. Breathing even, thoughts in order.
Rattled. Jumping at drips and shadows; hands not quite steady.
Fraying. Tunnel vision, snap decisions, the urge to just run somewhere, anywhere.
Panicking. The player acts before thinking — loud, fast, and visible to everything.

values.text: the Runoff strain, the harbor's oldest. It moves fast through warm blood, and the tint climbs the forearms in fine green veins
the Deep strain. It settles slowly and deep, and the skin over it stays cold long after a remedy has done its work
the Lantern strain. In the dark, the changed skin gives off a faint green glow that slimes and patrols both notice
the Echo strain. It carries sound, so the player sometimes hears slimes moving two streets away

entities.name: Green Slime
entities.playerDescription: A knee-high mound of luminous green that moves like poured glass. Slow, patient, and always slightly closer than it was.
entities.aiDescription: The Green Slime: a viscous, bioluminescent mass that flows over pavement like poured glass, leaving a faintly glowing trail. Drawn to warmth and motion, it tries to flow over and around a victim — skin it touches comes away tingling, cold, and a shade greener (Assimilation rises on contact). It recoils hard from salt, and it hesitates before striking anyone the change has already half-claimed. Slow enough to outwalk, patient enough that outwalking is never quite the end of it.
entities.aiSummary: Green Slime: slow luminous pursuer; contact spreads assimilation, salt repels it.
entities.imageTags: glowing green slime blob, wet asphalt, night fog, luminous trail

entities.name: Amber Creeper
entities.playerDescription: A honey-colored sheet that keeps to ceilings, gantries, and the undersides of fire escapes. You hear it only after it lets go.
entities.aiDescription: The Amber Creeper: a thin honey-colored slime that travels ceilings, gantries, and the undersides of fire escapes, patient as weather. It attacks by releasing its grip and falling in a heavy, enveloping sheet — the danger is above, always above. Slower than the green to spread the change, but far harder to peel off. Salt works; panic does not.
entities.aiSummary: Amber Creeper: ceiling-dwelling ambusher that drops in sheets; salt works, panic does not.
entities.imageTags: amber translucent slime sheet on ceiling, industrial gantry, dripping, night

entities.name: The Bloom
entities.playerDescription: The first pool, filling the flooded basement of the Works. Vast, calm, and lit from within. It is not hunting anyone. It doesn’t need to.
entities.aiDescription: The Bloom: the first and greatest slime, filling the flooded basement of the Chemical Works — vast, still, and glowing softly, the source every street slime traces back to. It does not hunt; it waits, and the city comes to it a person at a time. It is strangely beautiful and entirely indifferent. The dispensary’s reagent stock sits at its edge: mixing and applying the cure there reverses the player’s assimilation and ends the story in triumph. The Bloom does not try to stop them — which is somehow worse.
entities.aiSummary: The Bloom: the vast calm source pool in the Works basement; the cure is mixed at its edge.
entities.imageTags: vast glowing green pool in flooded industrial basement, still surface, soft light, catwalk above

entities.name: {{ph:df2b66a8-69e4-4b75-ab96-f75beb51a872:world:011c84f3-5319-4552-a333-b321af8da2a0:sName}}
entities.playerDescription: Your neighbor — sixty percent slime for a week now and oddly serene about it. These days they {{ph:df2b66a8-69e4-4b75-ab96-f75beb51a872:world:e9b31942-7ed6-4104-b1d1-44ab0dc70326:sHabit}}. Gives advice that is about forty percent useful.
entities.aiDescription: {{ph:df2b66a8-69e4-4b75-ab96-f75beb51a872:world:b0dcfd77-5697-4693-bce8-026767a0cb32:sName}}, the player's neighbor on Crescent Row: half-assimilated for over a week and long past panicking about it — translucent to the elbows, faintly luminous, calmly keeping up their routines: lately they {{ph:df2b66a8-69e4-4b75-ab96-f75beb51a872:world:21a92b22-f4ba-4757-b4c7-720dcc9d885b:sHabit}}. They know more about living with the change than any doctor: what slows it, what feeds it, and what the slimes do and don't notice. Their advice is dry, unhurried, and about forty percent useful. They are the picture of where the player's road ends if the cure stays unfound — and they seem okay with that, which should not be comforting.
entities.aiSummary: The neighbor: serenely half-assimilated local who knows how to live with the change.
entities.imageTags: middle-aged person with faintly translucent green-tinged arms, bathrobe, watering can, foggy night porch

values.text: mow the lawn at midnight, a faint green glow trailing the mower
bake for the whole street and never mention that the bread comes out translucent
sit on the porch singing to the storm drains, and something down there sings back
keep a careful notebook of how the change feels, and offer to read from it

entities.name: Quarantine Watch
entities.playerDescription: Municipal contractors in taped-up rain suits, running the cordon on triple overtime. Polite, exhausted, and very interested in your wrists.
entities.aiDescription: Quarantine Watch: municipal contractors in taped-up rain suits and fogged face shields, holding the cordon on triple overtime. They are not villains — they are tired people with clipboards, flashlights, and a containment list. They screen for visible signs (translucency, green tint, the smooth-jointed walk) and detain the visibly changed for transport to the containment site, politely and irreversibly. They can be talked to, distracted, and occasionally moved to look away — they were all somebody's neighbor last month.
entities.aiSummary: Quarantine Watch: tired cordon patrols who detain the visibly infected.
entities.imageTags: quarantine workers in taped rain suits, face shields, flashlights, foggy checkpoint, sawhorse barriers

entities.name: Hollis Pratt
entities.playerDescription: A retired veterinarian behind the Night Pharmacy counter, reading glasses on a chain. She rations the remedies and asks hard questions first.
entities.aiDescription: Hollis Pratt is a retired veterinarian who walked into the Night Pharmacy when the clerk walked out, and has kept the counter since. She rations the iodine and the electrolyte salts to whoever answers her questions honestly, and she treats people the way she treated dogs: firmly, kindly, and without discussion. Her father mixed reagents at the Chemical Works, so she knows the cure exists and which labels to look for in the dispensary. She will tell the player what she knows in exchange for help with something she wants done.
entities.aiSummary: Hollis Pratt: retired vet who rations the Night Pharmacy remedies and knows which reagents make the cure.
entities.imageTags: older woman with reading glasses on a chain, cardigan, pharmacy counter at night, fluorescent light

entities.name: The Loudspeakers
entities.playerDescription: Horn speakers on every third pole, looping the city's calm advice into the fog.
entities.aiDescription: The Loudspeakers: municipal horn speakers on poles across Ashburn, wired to one recorded voice that stays calm about everything. They loop curfew reminders, damp-report hotlines and reassurances nobody asked for, and every message ends: "{{ph:4756330b-6425-4097-bd86-ce38669df7b2:world:f8780960-99c1-42a4-93c1-e6165f8460f1}}" When the city changes its advice, the speakers announce it here first.
entities.aiSummary: The Loudspeakers: the city broadcast that loops calm advisories over every district.
entities.imageTags: municipal horn loudspeakers on a pole, fog, night, green haze, art deco city

dictionaries.name: The Ashburn Bulletin
dictionaries.description: Outbreak-night doctrine: how the slime works, how the cordon works, and how the story ends.

entries.name: Outbreak Night
entries.value: Ashburn on outbreak night is eerie, hushed and dryly funny: fog, green light and municipal understatement. Slimes coat and absorb; injuries are ordinary bumps and strains. The change is told clinically, through temperature, translucency, texture and grip. The danger is being claimed, filed or lost.

entries.name: The Change
entries.value: Assimilation climbs with every story hour and jumps on slime contact. The middle of the change helps: the body compresses through gaps bones should forbid, and slimes hesitate at someone half like them. The far end is erosion: failing grip, a blurred outline, memories arriving syrupy and out of order. Remedies, rest in dry warmth and salt-scrubbing push it back.

entries.name: Salt
entries.value: Every slime recoils from salt. A thrown handful buys seconds; a salted doorway holds all night; a salt-scrubbed patch of skin stings and clears. The whole city has quietly emptied its diners of shakers.

entries.name: The Cordon
entries.value: Quarantine Watch detains the visibly changed — politely, apologetically, and permanently — for transport to the containment site. They screen wrists and temples at checkpoints and log descriptions of anyone who refuses. Covered skin, shadow, and confident boredom get a person through; visible translucency under a checkpoint light does not.

entries.name: The Broadcast
entries.value: The municipal loudspeakers loop calm, faintly absurd advisories: curfew reminders, damp-report hotlines, reassurances nobody asked for. Every message ends the same way: "{{ph:4756330b-6425-4097-bd86-ce38669df7b2:world:2d8114d7-e9b5-422f-958a-14d4f61d43b6}}"

entries.name: The Works
entries.value: The outbreak traces to the derelict Chemical Works on the harbor, where decades of runoff pooled in the flooded basement and, one night, moved. Graffiti and radio agree on one thing: {{ph:f36a86e6-3977-4cc2-9a2e-3d58bd129d53:world:f4a5cee0-e389-4b17-85c7-9abdc2bee188}}. The dispensary's untouched reagent stock is mixed into the cure at the Bloom's edge, and applying it reverses the player's assimilation. Hollis Pratt at the Night Pharmacy knows which labels to look for.

entries.name: The Shelter
entries.value: Ashburn High's gym holds the district's evacuees: cots, thermoses, clipboard volunteers, and a screening line at the door. It is warm, dry, and safe from slimes — and the most dangerous room in the city for anyone hiding a green tint.

entries.name: Slime Habits
entries.value: Slimes are drawn to warmth and motion and calm around the half-changed. They flow over a person and coat them. They are unhurried, because the night is long and the city is not going anywhere.

values.text: the harbor glowed for three nights before the first pool moved
someone flushed something they shouldn't have
the plant's night watchman never clocked out in '86
the rain tasted sweet the week before it started
Ashburn thanks you for your compliance.
Remember: damp is not doom, but do report it.
This message repeats until it doesn’t.
